post_title: How many people will have applied to Kyrgyzstan's CEC to run in the January 2027 presidential election by the close of nominations (13 November 2026)?

question.title: How many people will have applied to Kyrgyzstan's CEC to run in the January 2027 presidential election by the close of nominations (13 November 2026)?
question.description:
Kyrgyzstan holds its regular presidential election on Wednesday, 27 January 2027. The Zhogorku Kenesh set that date on 24 September 2026 and the Central Commission for Elections and Referendums (CEC) approved the campaign calendar on 25 September 2026: nomination of candidates began the day after the decision was published, applications are accepted until 24:00 on 12 November 2026, the nomination stage closes on 13 November 2026, signature collection ends on 8 December 2026, and candidate registration closes on 23 December 2026 ([CEC election calendar](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/election/vybory-yanvar-2027/schedule/)). A candidate may be nominated either by a political party or by self-nomination; to be registered a candidate must be at least 35 years old, have lived in the country for 15 years, pass a state-language test, submit 30,000–60,000 voter signatures collected electronically, and pay a 1 million som electoral deposit.

Filing itself is cheap and broad, so application numbers are much larger than the eventual candidate list. In the 2017 presidential election the CEC received 59 applications, of which 9 were withdrawn and 37 rejected, leaving 13 registered candidates — 5 party-nominated and 8 self-nominated ([OSCE/ODIHR interim report](https://cdn.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/0/3/346966.pdf)). In the 2021 early presidential election, 65 individuals submitted nomination documents and 18 were registered ([OSCE/ODIHR final report](https://cdn.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/7/0/488587_1.pdf)). Both cycles thus saw roughly 60 filings, most from self-nominees who later failed at the signature or vetting stage.

The 2027 field has been slow to form. The first application arrived on 14 October 2026, and by 28 October 2026 the CEC reported three applicants, all self-nominated: businessman Aimen Kasenov (14 October; he also ran in 2021 and won 0.91% of the vote), Azamat Esenbekov (27 October), and Syimyk Zhapykeev (28 October, after retaking and passing the state-language test) ([24.kg](https://24.kg/en/article/presidential-election-syimyk-zhapykeev-announces-his-candidacy)). The state-language test now appears to gate filing itself — Zhapykeev only filed after passing it — which may make the ~60-filing totals of 2017 and 2021 less directly comparable to 2026. Other figures, including former interior minister Omurbek Suvanaliev, have publicly signalled that they intend to run.

President Sadyr Japarov, who won the January 2021 election with 79.2%, announced in August 2026 that he intends to seek a second term. In an interview published on 28 October 2026 he said that "quite a few candidates" would register by 13 November, that each of them would be a serious rival, and that administrative resources would not be used ([24.kg](https://24.kg/article/ya-nikogo-ne-prizyval-golosovat-za-menya-sadyr-zhaparov-otvetil-na-obvineniya)); he had not submitted his own application as of that date. His regional meetings with the population have already prompted complaints that he is campaigning early, which he rejects.

The CEC announces each new application and periodically gives a running total on its [news page](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/news/), with a dedicated [2027 election section](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/vybory-prezidenta-kr-2027/). In past Kyrgyz presidential races the bulk of applications arrived in the final days of the nomination window, so the count after five weeks (three filings) is a poor guide to the total at the deadline — the size of the last-minute surge is what this question turns on.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number of distinct persons from whom Kyrgyzstan's Central Commission for Elections and Referendums (CEC) received an application to be nominated as a candidate in the 27 January 2027 presidential election during the official nomination period — i.e., the CEC's final count of applications accepted in that period, which the CEC's [election calendar](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/election/vybory-yanvar-2027/schedule/) shows ending on 13 November 2026 (the CEC has also given 24:00 on 12 November 2026 as the cut-off for submitting applications; the CEC's final total controls either way). The answer is the final figure the CEC publishes after the nomination period on its [news page](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/news/) or its [2027 election section](https://shailoo.gov.kg/ru/vybory-prezidenta-kr-2027/); if the CEC states no aggregate figure, count the distinct persons on the CEC's list of citizens who submitted applications; if neither is available, use the figure the CEC gives to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Party-nominated and self-nominated candidates both count, each person is counted once even if they file more than once, and a person whose application the CEC recorded counts even if it was later withdrawn or refused. A person whose documents the CEC declined to accept at intake does not count. For example, if the CEC reports that 17 citizens had submitted applications, the question resolves to 17.
question.fine_print: Where the CEC reports both the number of applications received and the number of applicants whose documents were confirmed compliant, the number of applications received is used. Later stages of the process — signature collection (deadline 8 December 2026), the 1 million som deposit and candidate registration (deadline 23 December 2026) — do not affect the answer. If the CEC's final figure appears later than 13 November 2026, the question resolves when it is published.
